content.title: About
content.content: Radicchio is a type of leaf chicory (Cichorium intybus var. foliosum) known for its slightly bitter flavor and striking red veins. Raw leaves are used in salads, appetizers, and as a garnish. It is rich in vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Radicchio belongs to the Asteraceae family and is closely related to Belgian endive.
The deep red veins contain anthocyanins, powerful antioxidant pigments.
In Italy, radicchio is considered the "king of salads" and is a staple of the Veneto region.
Raw leaves retain more vitamin C than when they are cooked.
Varieties range from light green to fully red, depending on the cultivar.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K supports blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamins A and C
items.content: Vitamin A promotes eye health, while vitamin C boosts immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is essential for cell division and especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Anthocyanins and polyphenols help combat free radicals, reducing the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Raw radicchio is low in calories but high in dietary fiber, contributing to satiety.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to radicchio, manifested as itching or swelling.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Radicchio contains oxalates, which in excess can contribute to kidney stone formation.

items.title: Bitterness
items.content: Large amounts may cause an unpleasant bitterness, which can be harsh on sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw radicchio is thinly sliced and added to mixed salads, sandwiches, pasta dishes, or used as a colorful garnish. A splash of lemon juice can mellow its bitterness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store radicchio in the refrigerator in a bag or container with a slight humidity. Use within 3–5 days to keep its crunch and vivid color.
